content.text: Other important characters include:The Capitol Effie Trinket: a woman from the Capitol sent to reap District 12's tributes. She is vain and frivolous, but like Haymitch, comes to truly care about Katniss and Peeta. Cinna: Katniss's Capitol-assigned stylist who helps her prepare for the Games. He also truly likes Katniss and avoids pomp in favor of sincere simplicity. He turns her into a figurehead using her clothing. District 12 Gale Hawthorne: Katniss's childhood best friend who helped Katniss learn how to fight and hunt. He is also in love with Katniss. Madge Undersee: a friend of Katniss's from District 12, who gives Katniss a Mockingjay pin for Katniss to take into the arena with her as Katniss's one allotted item from home. Mockingjays are seen as symbols of hope, and Katniss will herself later be called the rebellion's Mockingjay. Madge is killed at the end of the second book. The cover of the novel depicts the Mockingjay pin Madge Undersee gives Katniss to take into the arena with her. To unlock this lesson you must be a Study.com Member. Create your account The Hunger Games is a dystopian trilogy by author Suzanne Collins. It consists of three books: The Hunger Games Catching Fire Mockingjay The books take place in the tyrannical nation of Panem, which consists of the controlling Capitol and twelve outer districts. Following the districts' rebellion, the Capitol began the annual practice of the Hunger Games., a gladiatorial contest where one boy and one girl from each of the twelve districts must fight to the death until only one victor remains. The tributes are chosen at the Reaping.The first book's major plot points include: To unlock this lesson you must be a Study.com Member. Create your account Imagining The Hunger GamesImagine a future world where the government controls nearly every aspect of your life—where you live and what you eat, where you're allowed to go and who you're allowed to talk to. Even your career is determined for you. To make matters even worse, the government has the right to pluck two children from your community and make them fight to the death on television. Sounds pretty horrible, right? For the characters in Suzanne Collins's The Hunger Games, this is the harsh reality of everyday life. PanemIf you've ever studied the ancient Romans, you may be familiar with the Latin phrase ''panem et circenses.'' It translates as ''bread and circuses.'' This idea was embraced by Roman emperors; so long as the Roman people were well fed and entertained, they could get away with doing whatever they wanted. The Hunger Games takes place in the futuristic Panem, a dystopian nation inspired by the Roman ''bread and circuses.'' Panem is made up of the Capitol and 12 economic regions called districts. Each district is responsible for a different economic activity. For example, District 1 (a favorite of the Capitol) manufactures luxury goods, District 4 is home to the country's fishing industry, and District 11 acts as the agricultural center of the country. While people living in the districts toil for long hours to earn slave wages, people living in the Capitol are cradled in the lap of luxury. They enjoy outrageous fashion trends, gorge themselves on decadent foods, and revel in the suffering of the districts. At this point, you're probably thinking to yourself, ''The Capitol sounds truly awful. How is it that the districts allow it to stay in power?'' The answer is really quite simple: the Hunger Games. Just over 70 years before the start of the book, Panem was caught in a nasty civil war. The districts rebelled against the Capitol, nearly causing the extinction of the human race. In the fighting, the Capitol destroyed the mysterious District 13, the home of nuclear development in Panem. After the rebellion was quashed, the Capitol created the Hunger Games to maintain peace and order by breeding fear in the districts. Every year, the Capitol goes to each of the 12 districts to ''reap'' the tributes, one boy and one girl between the ages of 12 and 18. The tributes are then sent to the Capitol, where they're primped and prepped to fight in a nationally televised fight to the death. Only one of the 24 tributes will survive. The winner is rewarded with immense riches and fame unlike anything they've seen before. Such prizes, however, can never truly make up for what they see and experience during the Hunger Games. The book The Hunger Games is told from the perspective of Katniss Everdeen, a 16 year old living in District 12, Panem's coal-mining region. The poorest of the districts, District 12 is largely neglected by the Capitol. The electric fence that contains the district is rarely electrified, and the local Peacekeepers, Panem's law enforcement, are friendly with the residents. Year after year, District 12 has a poor showing in the Hunger Games. The people of the Capitol don't expect much of District 12's tributes—that is, until they meet Katniss. CharactersSuzanne Collins's novel The Hunger Games is filled with dynamic, exciting, and sometimes awful characters. As mentioned before, Katniss Everdeen is the heroine and narrator of The Hunger Games. Katniss is an avid hunter, something she learned from her father. After Mr. Everdeen died in a tragic mine explosion, Katniss has acted as the primary caretaker for her family, making sure there's enough food on the table. When Katniss's sister, Primrose, is reaped for the Hunger Games, Katniss bravely volunteers to take her place. Through the rest of the novel, Katniss defies the Capitol and beats the odds to survive the Hunger Games along with fellow victor Peeta Mellark. Katniss's heroism and bravery make her a national icon and the face of rebellion against the Capitol. Primrose Everdeen, popularly known as ''Prim,'' is Katniss's little sister. Prim is young and sweet. She loves her cat, Buttercup, and also has a pet goat. Along with Katniss, Peeta Mellark is reaped to compete in the Hunger Games. Peeta is the son of a baker in District 12. Unbeknownst to Katniss, Peeta has loved her since they were children. This information comes out on national television during a pre-Games interview. At the start of the Hunger Games, Katniss suspects that Peeta has aligned himself with tributes from strong districts so he can hunt her down and kill her. In reality, Peeta does this to protect her. Eventually, Peeta and Katniss partner up and survive the Hunger Games together. Gale Hawthorne is Katniss's best friend and closest confidante. Gale's father died in the same mining accident as Mr. Everdeen, and Gale hunts alongside Katniss to support his family as well. After Katniss is reaped for the Hunger Games, Gale realizes his true feelings for her. While she's off competing, Gale promises to take care of her family (and to continue doing so if she doesn't return).
